findings.passage: Contrary to that oath, House Democrats called up four gun-control bills for votes this week, and I voted “no” on every one of them.
findings.note: Op-ed on his official House site stating he voted no on four gun-control bills, citing the U.S. and Pennsylvania constitutions.

findings.passage: The Red Flag law (House Bill 1859) would have allowed for a person’s firearm to be confiscated without due process. This is a clear violation of both the U.S. and Pennsylvania constitutions.
findings.note: His statement on the red-flag bill HB 1859.

findings.passage: House Bill 1099 would have ended the time-honored tradition of gun owners building firearms by limiting the types of materials that could be used to construct firearms and prohibited the right of individuals to build their own firearms at home.

House Bill 1866 would have banned “a part or combination of parts designed and intended to simulate the rate of fire of a machine gun.” No explanation of what “simulate the rate of fire of a machine gun” meant was ever offered, leading to the potential for broad and misguided enforcement.

Despite the success in stopping the previous, unconstitutional bills, I am disappointed a bill to expand background check requirements to include private sales of long guns, such as hunting rifles and shotguns, narrowly passed. I am hopeful House Bill 1593 will not be taken up by the Senate.
findings.note: His statement on HB 1593 (background checks on private long-gun sales).

findings.passage: The stated policy positions of each of these bills are already covered by existing state and federal laws, and enactment of any of these pieces of legislation would only curb the rights of law-abiding citizens.
findings.note: His general reason for opposing the four bills.

findings.passage: “The upcoming seminar offers a valuable chance for residents to better understand their rights and responsibilities as gun owners,” Reichard said.
findings.note: Official press release quote about a concealed-carry seminar he hosted with the county sheriff.

findings.passage: He is a fiscal conservative who believes wasteful government spending must be eliminated and is a defender of firearm owner rights, medical freedom and parental rights in education.
findings.note: Biography on his official site, written in the third person by his office.
